nodes.name: NLS with inverse-square potential (1.1)
nodes.statement: i\partial_t u + \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u &= 0, \quad u(0,\cdot)=u_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),
nodes.statement_short: Focusing NLS with attractive inverse-square potential $c|x|^{-2}$ and $H^1$ initial data.
nodes.label: inls

nodes.name: Hardy constant $c_*$
nodes.statement: We shall fix the coupling constant $c\in(0,c_*)$, where $c_*=(N-2)^2/4$ is the best constant in Hardy's inequality: \begin{equation} c_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \leqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2 dx, \quad u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fix $c\in(0,c_*)$, $c_*=(N-2)^2/4$ the best constant in Hardy's inequality.

nodes.name: Hardy's inequality
nodes.statement: c_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \leqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2 dx, \quad u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N).
conclusions: c_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \leqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2 dx
nodes.label: hardy

nodes.name: strong solution and maximal existence time $T$
nodes.statement: We consider strong solutions $u=u(t,x)\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^N)$, where $T>0$ is the maximum time of existence of $u$.

nodes.name: mass and energy
nodes.statement: Along the flow of~\eqref{inls}, we have conservation of the $L^2$ norm, also known as the \emph{mass}: \begin{equation} \Vert u(t)\Vert_{L^2_x} \equiv \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2_x}, \end{equation} and of the \emph{energy}: \begin{equation} E(u(t))=\frac12 \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\,\mathrm{d} x - \frac{c}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u(t,x)|^2}{|x|^2}dx - \frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u(t,x)|^{p+1}\,\mathrm{d} x \equiv E(u_0). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Mass ($L^2$ norm) and energy $E(u)$ of a solution, both conserved along the flow.

nodes.name: mass conservation (1.3)
nodes.statement: \Vert u(t)\Vert_{L^2_x} \equiv \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2_x},
nodes.label: mass

nodes.name: energy conservation (1.4)
nodes.statement: E(u(t))=\frac12 \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\,\mathrm{d} x - \frac{c}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u(t,x)|^2}{|x|^2}dx - \frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u(t,x)|^{p+1}\,\mathrm{d} x \equiv E(u_0).
nodes.label: energy

nodes.name: global solution
nodes.statement: A solution is called global if $T=+\infty$.

nodes.name: Local well-posedness (Okazawa-Suzuki-Yokota)
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$. For any initial value $u_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^N)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$. Moreover, the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$. Finally, if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
conclusions: there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^N)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$
if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$
if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global
nodes.statement_short: Local well-posedness in $H^1$ with conservation laws, blow-up alternative, and global existence for $L^2$-subcritical $p$.
nodes.label: local.thm

nodes.name: symmetries of the NLS (time translation, phase, scaling)
nodes.statement: More precisely, if $u(t,x)$ solves~\eqref{inls}, then so do: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $u_{t_0}(t,x)=u(t-t_0,x)$, for all $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$ (time translation invariance); \item $u_{\gamma_0}(t,x)=e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$, for all $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ (phase invariance); \item $u_{\lambda_0}(t,x)=\lambda_0^{2/(p-1)}u(\lambda_0^2t,\lambda_0x)$, for all $\lambda_0>0$ (scaling invariance). \end{enumerate}
conclusions: $u_{\gamma_0}(t,x)=e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$
$u_{\lambda_0}(t,x)=\lambda_0^{2/(p-1)}u(\lambda_0^2t,\lambda_0x)$
nodes.statement_short: Solutions are preserved by time translation, phase rotation and scaling.

nodes.name: Hardy functional
nodes.statement: For our analysis it is convenient to introduce the {\em Hardy functional}, defined on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ by \[ H(u)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2dx -c\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx. \]

nodes.name: Hardy functional equivalence (1.5)
nodes.statement: \left(1-\frac{c}{c_*}\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2dx\leqslant H(u)\leqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\nabla u|^2dx.
nodes.label: hardy2

nodes.name: $L^2$ scaling
nodes.statement: Now, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$ yields $2/(p-1)=N/2$ and, as in the classical case $c=0$, \eqref{inls} is invariant under the {\em $L^2$ scaling} \[ u(t,x) \to u_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2 t, \lambda x) \quad (\lambda>0). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $p=1+4/N$ the equation is invariant under $u_\lambda=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2t,\lambda x)$.

nodes.name: $L^2$ critical
nodes.statement: This transformation preserves the $L^2$ norm and \eqref{inls} is called {\em $L^2$ critical}.

nodes.name: standing waves and the stationary equation
nodes.statement: Indeed, $u(t,x)=e^{it}\varphi(x)$ is a (global) solution of~\eqref{inls} if and only if $\varphi\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation \begin{equation} \Delta\varphi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\varphi - \varphi + |\varphi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\varphi=0. \end{equation}
conclusions: $u(t,x)=e^{it}\varphi(x)$ is a (global) solution of~\eqref{inls} if and only if $\varphi\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation
equivalent_conditions: $\varphi\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation
nodes.statement_short: Standing waves $e^{it}\varphi$ solve the NLS iff $\varphi$ solves the stationary elliptic equation (1.6).

nodes.name: stationary equation (1.6)
nodes.statement: \Delta\varphi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\varphi - \varphi + |\varphi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\varphi=0.
nodes.label: sinls

nodes.name: uniqueness of the ground state for $c=0$
nodes.statement: For $c=0$, it is well known that the ground state is unique, up to the symmetries of \eqref{sinls}. More precisely, there exists a unique positive radial solution $Q\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ of \eqref{sinls}, and $\mathcal{G}=\{e^{i\gamma_0}Q(\cdot - x_0) : \gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}, \ x_0\in\mathbb{R}^N\}$.
conclusions: there exists a unique positive radial solution $Q\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ of \eqref{sinls}, and $\mathcal{G}=\{e^{i\gamma_0}Q(\cdot - x_0) : \gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}, \ x_0\in\mathbb{R}^N\}$

nodes.name: uniqueness of ground states for $c>0$
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, for $c>0$, we are not aware of any uniqueness result for \eqref{sinls} on $\mathbb{R}^N$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness of the ground state of (1.6) for $c>0$ is unknown.

nodes.name: Sharp global well-posedness
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$. If $u_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}, \end{equation} then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
conclusions: the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global
nodes.statement_short: Solutions with mass below the ground-state mass $M_{gs}$ are global.
nodes.label: global.thm

nodes.name: subcritical mass condition (1.7)
nodes.statement: \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs},
nodes.label: sharp

nodes.name: proof sketch of sharp global well-posedness
nodes.statement: The proof of this theorem relies on the inequality \begin{equation} E(u)\geqslant \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N), \end{equation} which follows from a sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality established in Section~\ref{global.sec}. Indeed, since the $L^2$ norm and the energy are conserved, \eqref{posE} immediately yields an \emph{a priori} bound on $H(u(t))$ --- and hence on $\Vert\nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}$ --- in the case $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}$. Namely, we have \begin{equation} H(u(t)) \leqslant 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1}, \end{equation} which implies global existence.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-based lower bound (1.8) on the energy plus conservation laws gives an a priori bound on $H(u(t))$.

nodes.name: energy lower bound (1.8)
nodes.statement: E(u)\geqslant \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),
nodes.label: posE

nodes.name: a priori bound on $H(u(t))$ (1.9)
nodes.statement: H(u(t)) \leqslant 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1},
nodes.label: subcritical

nodes.name: minimal mass blow-up family $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$
nodes.statement: Taking into account the above symmetries of~\eqref{inls} we obtain, for each ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, a 3-parameter family $(S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0})_{T\in\mathbb{R},\lambda_0>0,\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}}$ of minimal mass solutions of~\eqref{inls} blowing up in finite time, defined as \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Three-parameter family of explicit blow-up solutions: pseudo-conformal transforms of rescaled, phase-shifted ground states.

nodes.name: explicit blow-up solutions (1.10)
nodes.statement: S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right).
nodes.label: S1.def

nodes.name: Classification of minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$. Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
assumptions: $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$
conclusions: there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
nodes.statement_short: Every minimal-mass solution blowing up at $T$ is an explicit pseudo-conformal ground-state solution $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$.
nodes.label: main.thm

nodes.name: local well-posedness at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: However, it is not clear to us that local well-posedness holds in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Local well-posedness of the NLS at the Hardy threshold $c=c_*$ is unclear.

nodes.name: Weinstein functional
nodes.statement: Consider the Weinstein functional \[ J^{p,N}(u):=\frac{H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|u\|^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}_{L^2}}{\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Existence of minimizers of the Weinstein functional
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$, \[ \alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u) \] is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation \begin{equation} N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0. \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \alpha_{p,N}=2\frac{\|Q\|_{L^2}^{p-1}}{p+1}. \end{equation} In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation
In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.statement_short: The infimum $\alpha_{p,N}$ of the Weinstein functional is attained at a positive radial solution $Q$ of the Euler-Lagrange equation.
nodes.label: minimization.prop

nodes.name: Euler-Lagrange equation (2.1)
nodes.statement: N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0.

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*} Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\geqslant0$. Since $J(|u|)\leqslant J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\geqslant0$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \geqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing. Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \geqslant 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\leqslant 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\leqslant 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\leqslant J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\leqslant \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$. Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\geqslant0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}. Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Direct method: symmetrize and rescale a minimizing sequence, use radial compactness and lower semicontinuity to get a minimizer, then solve its Euler-Lagrange equation.

nodes.name: Euler-Lagrange equation of $J^{p,N}$ (2.3)
nodes.statement: -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: euler

nodes.name: critical Euler-Lagrange equation (2.4)
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: euler2

nodes.name: phase invariance and mass of minimizers
nodes.statement:
oindent (a) Note that, by phase invariance of $J^{p,N}$, if $u$ is a minimizer so is $e^{i	heta}u, \ 	heta\in\mathbb{R}$. \medskip 
oindent (b) For $p=1+ rac{4}{N}$, the Pohozaev identity for \eqref{sinls} implies that any minimizer $u$ of $J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}$ satisfies $E(u)=0$, that is \[ H(u)= rac{1}{1+ rac{2}{N}}\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}, \] and so  egin{equation} J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}(u) = rac{H(u)\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}} = rac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{1+ rac{2}{N}}. \end{equation} Therefore, all minimizers have the same mass. \medskip 
oindent (c) The proof of Proposition~ef{charact.prop} below shows that all minimizers are positive and radial, up to a global phase factor.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers are phase invariant; for $p=1+4/N$, Pohozaev gives $E=0$ so all minimizers have the same mass.
nodes.label: gs_scaling.rem

nodes.name: value of $J$ at a minimizer (2.5)
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: valueofmin

nodes.name: ground states and minimal mass
nodes.statement: In the case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, we call {\em ground states} the minimizers of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$ that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}. We denote the set of ground states by $\mathcal{G}$. In view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem}~(b), there exists $M_\mathrm{gs}>0$ such that $\Vert Q\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ for all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$. We call $M_\mathrm{gs}$ the {\em minimal mass}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Ground states: positive radial minimizers of $J$ solving (1.6); their common mass is the minimal mass $M_{gs}$.
nodes.label: gs.def

nodes.name: $L^2$ scaling of ground states
nodes.statement: The $L^2$ scaling $u_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda{x})$ yields \[ H(u_\lambda)=\lambda^2H(u), \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}, \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}=\lambda^2 \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}, \quad \text{hence} \quad J^{p,N}(u_\lambda)=J^{p,N}(u). \] Therefore, if $Q$ is a ground state, then $Q_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x)$ is again a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, satisfying $\Vert Q_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and the rescaled Euler--Lagrange equation \[ \Delta Q_\lambda+ \frac{c}{|x|^2}Q_\lambda-\lambda^{2} Q_\lambda + |Q_\lambda|^{\frac{4}{N}}Q_\lambda=0. \] It follows from Remark~\ref{minmass.rem} below that the ground states are the solutions of \eqref{sinls} with smallest mass.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: $L^2$ rescalings of a ground state are again minimizers with the same mass, solving a rescaled equation.
nodes.label: scaling.rem

nodes.name: derivation of the sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: The following sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality is an immediate consequence of Proposition~\ref{minimization.prop}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the minimization result of Proposition 1.

nodes.name: sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$ and $u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, we have \begin{equation} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \leqslant \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}, \end{equation} where \[ \alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}} \quad\text{in the critical case} \quad p=1+\frac{4}{N}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: \begin{equation} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \leqslant \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality with the Hardy functional; constant given by the ground-state mass in the critical case.
nodes.label: GN.cor

nodes.name: Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality (2.6)
nodes.statement: \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \leqslant \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)},
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: GN

nodes.name: proof of Theorem 2 (sharp global well-posedness)
nodes.statement: ~{\it Theorem~\ref{global.thm}}. Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded. We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \] Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\leqslant \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\textstyle\frac2N)\displaystyle\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \] Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\leqslant 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\leqslant}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\leqslant 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: By the blow-up alternative, bound $H(u(t))$: sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg plus conservation of mass and energy give an a priori bound.

nodes.name: $L^2$ critical nonlinearity from Section 3 on
nodes.statement: From now on and for the rest of the paper, unless specified otherwise, we focus on the $L^2$ critical nonlinearity $p=1+\frac4N$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: pseudo-conformal transformation
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}. Then, for all $T\in\mathbb{R}$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
conclusions: for all $T\in\mathbb{R}$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$
nodes.statement_short: The pseudo-conformal transform of a global solution is a mass-preserving solution on $(-\infty,T)$.
nodes.label: pseudo-conf.lem

nodes.name: proof of the pseudo-conformal lemma
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \Delta u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\Delta u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives. For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \] It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of the derivatives, nonlinear and potential terms of $u_T$.

nodes.name: ground states have the smallest mass among stationary solutions
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} that any solution $\varphi$ of \eqref{sinls} satisfies $\|\varphi\|_{L^2}\geqslant M_\mathrm{gs}$. Otherwise, applying Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} with $u(t,x)=e^{it}\varphi(x)$, one could construct a finite time blow-up solution below the minimal mass threshold, which would contradict our global well-posedness result, Theorem~\ref{global.thm}.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Any solution of (1.6) has mass at least $M_{gs}$, else the pseudo-conformal transform would contradict Theorem 2.
nodes.label: minmass.rem

nodes.name: explicit minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: For all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $T\in\mathbb{R}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$, the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right), \end{equation} is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
conclusions: is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$
nodes.statement_short: Each $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ is a minimal-mass solution blowing up at $T$ with rate $C/(T-t)$.
nodes.label: blow-up_sol.prop

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement: The proposition is a simple consequence of Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} applied to the global solution \[ u_{Q,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\lambda_0^2 t}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x), \] which is given by applying the scaling and phase symmetries to the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{it}Q(x)$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Apply the pseudo-conformal lemma to the rescaled, phase-shifted standing wave.

nodes.name: all blow-up solutions come from one solution $S$
nodes.statement: Note that the blow-up solutions of the family exhibited in Proposition~\ref{blow-up_sol.prop} can all be retrieved from the solution \[ S(t,x) := S_{0,1,0}(t,x) = e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4t}} e^{-\frac{i}{t}} \frac{1}{|t|^{N/2}}Q\left(-\frac{x}{t}\right), \] defined on $(-\infty,0)$ and which blows up at $t=0$ with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{|t|}\quad \text{as } t\uparrow0, \] for some $C>0$. Indeed, all the solutions $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are equal to $S$, up to the symmetries (a), (b) and (c) stated in the introduction. Namely, if we apply the changes $u(t,x)\to \lambda_0^{-N/2}u(\lambda_0^{-2}t,\lambda_0^{-1}x)$, $u(t,x)\to u(t-T,x)$ and finally $u(t,x)\to e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$ to $S$, we obtain $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: All $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are images of a single solution $S$ under the symmetries.

nodes.name: Variational characterization of ground states
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ be such that \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0. \end{equation} Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\displaystyle\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
conclusions: there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$
nodes.statement_short: Functions with minimal mass and zero energy are rescaled, phase-shifted ground states.
nodes.label: charact.prop

nodes.name: minimal mass and zero energy (4.1)
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0.
nodes.label: varchar

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement:
It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+ rac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)\leqslant J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer. Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization. Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert 
abla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant \Vert

Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad 	ext{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big( rac{2}{N}\Big)^{ rac{1}{2}} rac{H(|v|)^ rac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \] The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $\mathbb{R}^N$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$. Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $\mathrm{Re}(\overline{w}
abla w)\equiv 0$, thus \[ |

abla(|v|)|^2+|v|^2|

abla(|v|)\cdot \mathrm{Re}(\overline{w}
abla w) \] and \[ \|

eq 0$ then $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction. Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: $v$ minimizes $J$; Schwarz symmetrization shows $|v|$ radial, so $|v|$ is a rescaled ground state; Hardy's inequality forces constant phase.

nodes.name: proof sketch of the concentration-compactness lemma
nodes.statement: Owing to the equivalence of the seminorms $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2$ and $H(u)$, the following concentration-compactness lemma can be proved by minor modifications to the proof of Proposition~1.7.6 in \cite{cazenave}.
nodes.statement_short: Minor modification of Cazenave's concentration-compactness proof, using equivalence of $H$ and $\|\nabla u\|^2$.

nodes.name: concentration-compactness lemma
nodes.statement:
Let $\{v_n\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}\subset H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ satisfy \[ \lim_{n ightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M<+\infty \quad 	ext{and} \quad \sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} H(v_n) <+\infty. \] Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ that satisfies one of the following properties. \medskip 
oindent (V) $\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^q}ightarrow 0$ as $kightarrow\infty$ for all $q\in(2,2^*)$. \medskip 
oindent (D) There are sequences ${w_k},{z_k}\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and a constant $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that:  egin{enumerate} \item $\mathrm{dist}(\mathrm{supp}(w_k),\mathrm{supp}(z_k))ightarrow\infty$; \item $|v_k|+|z_k|\leqslant |v_{n_k}|$; \item $\sup_{k\in\mathbb{N}} (\|w_k\|_{H^1}+\|z_k\|_{H^1})<+\infty$; \item $\|w_k\|_{L^2}ightarrow\alpha M$ and $\|z_k\|_{L^2}	o (1-\alpha)M$ as $kightarrow\infty$; \item $\lim_{kightarrow\infty} ig| \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|^q-\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^q-\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|z_k|^q ig|=0$ for all $q\in[2,2^*)$; \item $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty} ig\{ H(v_{n_k})-H(w_k)-H(z_k)  ig\}\geqslant 0$. \end{enumerate} \medskip 
oindent (C) There exists $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ such that \[ v_{n_k}(\cdot -y_k)ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(\mathbb{R}^N), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*). \]
conclusions: there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ that satisfies one of the following properties.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded sequences admit a subsequence that vanishes (V), dichotomizes (D) or is compact up to translations (C).
nodes.label: conc-comp.lemma

nodes.name: compactness of minimizing sequences
nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $\{v_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ satisfying \begin{equation} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}, \quad 0<\limsup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}H(v_n)<+\infty, \quad \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}E(v_n)\leqslant 0. \end{equation} Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$, $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0. \end{equation}
conclusions: there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$, $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sequences at the minimal mass with nonpositive limiting energy converge in $H^1$, up to subsequence and phase, to a ground state.
nodes.label: compact.prop

nodes.name: hypotheses on $\{v_n\}$ (4.2)
nodes.statement: \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}, \quad 0<\limsup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}H(v_n)<+\infty, \quad \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}E(v_n)\leqslant 0.
nodes.label: a

nodes.name: $H^1$ convergence to a ground state (4.3)
nodes.statement: \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0.
nodes.label: compact

nodes.name: proof of Proposition 4 (compactness)
nodes.statement:
The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $\mathbb{R}^N$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~ef{charact.prop}. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(\mathbb{R}^N)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\Big\{ rac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})- rac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}= rac{1}{2}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[  egin{split} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\leqslant rac{1}{2}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) - rac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|dx \ &\leqslant\limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\leqslant 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (ef{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\geqslant 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad 	ext{and} \quad E(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad	ext{and}\quad H(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|z_k|^{p+1}dxight)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$. Consequently, by Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ such that  egin{equation} \widetilde{v}_{n_k} ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(\mathbb{R}^N), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \widetilde{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\widetilde{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\widetilde{v}_{n_k}ightharpoonup v$ weakly in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2: Localization.} We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|ightarrow\infty$ as $kightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}. We start by showing that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\geqslant R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$, there exists $C\geqslant0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\leqslant R^{-2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\leqslant CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$. Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\geqslant\delta. \end{equation*} Note that this inequality will still hold if we increase the value of $R$ or pass to a further subsequence. Let $a>0$ and $\varphi\in C_0^\infty([0,\infty))$ be such that $\varphi(r)=1$ for $0\leqslant r \leqslant R$, $\varphi(r)=0$ for $r\geqslant R+a$, $0\leqslant\varphi\leqslant1$ and $\|\varphi'\|_{L^\infty}\leqslant 1/a$. Then define \[ u_k(x)=\varphi(|x|) v_{n_k}(x) \quad	ext{and}\quad w_k(x)=(1-\varphi(|x|))v_{n_k}(x). \] We clearly have $|u_k|,|w_k|\leqslant|v_{n_k}|$, and $\{u_k\},\{w_k\}\subset H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ with \[ |
abla u_k|^2 \leqslant 2\left((\varphi')^2|v_{n_k}|^2+\varphi^2|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \leqslant 2\left(a^{-2}|v_{n_k}|^2+|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \] and \[ |
abla w_k|^2 \leqslant 2\left((\varphi')^2|v_{n_k}|^2+(1-\varphi)^2|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \leqslant 2\left(a^{-2}|v_{n_k}|^2+|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight). \] Furthermore,  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} rac{|u_k|^2}{|x|^2}dx\geqslant \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\geqslant\delta, \end{equation*} and \eqref{hardy} yields  egin{equation} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(u_k)=\liminf_{kightarrow\infty} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |
abla u_k|^2dx-c\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} rac{|u_k|^2}{|x|^2}dxight) \geqslant (c_*-c)\delta>0. \end{equation} Using the sequences $\{u_k\},\{w_k\}$, we can now rewrite $H(v_{n_k})$ as  egin{align*} H(v_{n_k}) &=H(u_k)+H(w_k) \ &\phantom{=}+\int_{R<|x|<R+a} \Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dx. \end{align*} We will show that there exist $R>0$ as large as we want and $a>0$ such that, up to a further subsequence,  egin{equation} \limsup_{k	o\infty}\left|\int_{R<|x|<R+a} \Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dxight|\leqslant rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{2}. \end{equation} Using \eqref{crucial}, this will imply  egin{equation} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) \geqslant\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)+ rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{2}>\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k), \end{equation} which will lead to the desired contradiction. To prove \eqref{est0}, we use the above properties of $u_k$ and $w_k$ to observe that  egin{multline} \left|\int_{R<|x|<R+a}\Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dxight| \ \leqslant 5\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|
abla v_{n_k}|^2dx+4a^{-2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx + rac{3c}{R^2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx. \end{multline} First, by choosing $R>0$ sufficiently large, we will have  egin{equation}  rac{3c}{R^2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx \leqslant  rac{3c}{R^2} \|v_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 \leqslant  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{4} \quad	ext{for all} \ k\in\mathbb{N}. \end{equation} The second term in the right-hand side of \eqref{est} is handled using Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$: for any fixed $R,a>0$, we have that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx=0. \end{equation} As for the first term, we claim that we can choose $R>0$ as large as we want and $a>0$ such that, up to a subsequence,  egin{equation} 5\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|
abla v_{n_k}|^2dx\leqslant  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{4} \quad	ext{for all} \ k\in\mathbb{N}. \end{equation} Estimates \eqref{term3}--\eqref{term1} prove \eqref{est0}, and hence \eqref{e1}. If the above claim is not true, then using a diagonal argument we can construct a subsequence $\{v_{n_{k_l}}\}$, and a sequence of pairwise disjoint annuli \[ A_j=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N : R_j<|x|<R_j+a_j\} \quad	ext{with}\quad R_{j+1}>R_j+a_j, \] such that, for all $j\in\{1,\dots,l\}$, \[ \int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx\geqslant  ar \delta:=  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{20}>0 \quad	ext{for all} \ n_{k_l}\in\mathbb{N}. \] But then \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \geqslant \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \geqslant \sum_{j=1}^l\int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \geqslant l ar\delta, \] and it follows that \[ \lim_{l	o\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx=+\infty. \] In view of \eqref{hardy2} this contradicts \eqref{a}, and completes the proof of \eqref{e1}. We will now combine \eqref{e1} with the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN} and the assumption on the energy in \eqref{a} to reach a contradiction. Using Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^{p+1}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Hence, by \eqref{a},  egin{align*} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})\leqslant rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx = rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx, \end{align*} and so, by \eqref{e1},  egin{align} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)< rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx. \end{align} Using again Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we also have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$, which implies \[ M_\mathrm{gs}=\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^2} =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|w_k\|_{L^2}. \] Therefore, \eqref{GN} applied to $w_k$ yields \[  rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx \leqslant\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\left( rac{\|w_k\|_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}ight)^{ rac4N}H(w_k) = \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k), \] which, together with \eqref{e4}, leads to the contradiction \[ \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)<\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k). \] This shows that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$ and completes the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We now have  egin{align*} \liminf_{k	o\infty} E(v_{n_k}) &=\liminf_{k	o\infty}  rac12 \|
abla v_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 -\lim_{k	o\infty}  rac{1}{p+1} \| v_{n_k}\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}\ &=\liminf_{k	o\infty}  rac12 \|
abla \widetilde{v}_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 -\lim_{k	o\infty}  rac{1}{p+1} \| \widetilde{v}_{n_k}\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}\ &\geqslant  rac12 \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2 -  rac{1}{p+1} \|v\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}>E(v)\geqslant 0, \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from \eqref{posE} with $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. This contradicts \eqref{a} and shows that the sequence $\{y_k\}$ must indeed be bounded in $\mathbb{R}^N$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~3: Conclusion.} Suppose, without loss of generality, that $y_k	o y^*\in\mathbb{R}^N$. Then \[ v_{n_k}	o v^*=v(\cdot+y^*) \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(\mathbb{R}^N), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*), \] and $v_{n_k}ightharpoonup v^*$ weakly in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since the Hardy functional $H$ is weakly lower semi-continuous \cite{montefusco}, and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, it now follows by \eqref{posE} that \[  egin{split} 0\leqslant E(v^*)= rac{1}{2}H(v^*)- rac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v^*|^{p+1}dx &\leqslant  rac{1}{2}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})- rac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v^*|^{p+1}dx\ &\phantom{\leqslant}=\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})\leqslant 0, \end{split} \] so in fact  egin{equation} E(v^*)=0 \quad	ext{and}\quad H(v^*)=\lim_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}). \end{equation} Since $\|v^*\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(v^*)=0$, Proposition ef{charact.prop} yields $v^*=e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}$ for some $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$, $\lambda_0>0$, and some $Q\in \mathcal{G}$. Finally, by \eqref{convergence} and \eqref{hardy2}, we also have that $\|v_{n_k}\|_{H^1}ightarrow \|v^*\|_{H^1}$. Hence $\{v_{n_k}\}$ converges strongly to $v^*$ in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Concentration-compactness: rule out vanishing and dichotomy, then prove the translations stay bounded by contradiction. The key step combines Hardy's inequality near the origin with the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality to show escaping mass gives positive energy.

nodes.statement: In the $L^2$ critical case, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, (\ref{virialtwo}) reduces to \begin{equation} \Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0). \end{equation}

nodes.statement_short: Expansion of $E(ue^{is\theta})$ in $s$.

nodes.name: Banica's lemma
nodes.statement_short: At the ground-state mass, the momentum-type integral is bounded by $\sqrt{2E(u)}$ times a weighted $L^2$ norm.

nodes.name: proof of Theorem 3 (classification)
nodes.statement_short: Rescale along $t_n\to T$ and apply compactness to show the mass concentrates at 0. Banica's lemma and the virial identities then give $\Gamma(t)=8E(u_0)(T-t)^2$, so $u_0e^{i|x|^2/4T}$ is a ground state and $u$ is the pseudo-conformal solution.

nodes.statement: \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0,

nodes.name: scaling invariance of $J$
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Show $J$ is invariant under $u\mapsto\mu u(\lambda x)$.

nodes.name: symmetrized minimizing sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\geqslant0$. Since $J(|u|)\leqslant J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\geqslant0$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \geqslant \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Take a minimizing sequence, made nonnegative and Schwarz symmetrized.

nodes.name: normalized minimizing sequence
nodes.statement: Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \geqslant 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Rescale to $\|\psi_n\|_2=H(\psi_n)=1$, bounded in $H^1$.

nodes.name: weak limit is a minimizer
nodes.statement: Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\leqslant 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\leqslant 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\leqslant J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\leqslant \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Radial compactness and lower semicontinuity show the weak limit attains $\alpha_{p,N}$.

nodes.name: Euler-Lagrange equation and $Q$
nodes.statement: Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\geqslant0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Write the Euler-Lagrange equation and rescale $\psi^*$ to $Q$ solving (2.1), (2.2).

nodes.name: critical case rescaling
nodes.statement: Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: For $p=1+4/N$ rescale minimizers into solutions of (1.6).

nodes.name: reduction to bounding $H$
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Reduce global existence to boundedness of $H(u(t))$ via the blow-up alternative.

nodes.name: energy identity for $H$
nodes.statement: We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Express $H$ through $E$ and the $L^{2+4/N}$ norm.

nodes.name: apply Gagliardo-Nirenberg
nodes.statement: Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\leqslant \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\textstyle\frac2N)\displaystyle\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \]
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Bound the nonlinear term by the sharp GN inequality.

nodes.name: a priori bound
nodes.statement: Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\leqslant 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\leqslant}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\leqslant 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.statement_short: Conservation laws give $(1-(\|u_0\|/M_{gs})^{4/N})H(u(t))\le 2E(u_0)$.

nodes.name: time and space derivatives
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \Delta u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\Delta u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\partial_t u_T$ and $\Delta u_T$.

nodes.name: nonlinear and potential terms
nodes.statement: For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \]
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Compute the nonlinear and potential terms of $u_T$.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.statement: It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get the equation for $u_T$.

nodes.name: $v$ and $|v|$ are minimizers
nodes.statement: It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)\leqslant J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer.
nodes.statement_short: By (2.5), $v$ and $|v|$ minimize $J$.

nodes.name: positive minimizers are radial
nodes.statement: Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization. Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \frac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert \nabla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant \Vert \nabla v_0\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\leqslant\Vert v_0\Vert_{L^2}, \] we get $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0^*)<J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0)$, a contradiction. We deduce that $|v|$ is radial.
nodes.statement_short: Strict Hardy-term increase under symmetrization shows positive minimizers are radial.

nodes.name: $|v|$ is a rescaled ground state
nodes.statement: Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad \text{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big(\frac{2}{N}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{H(|v|)^\frac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Via the Euler-Lagrange equation, $|v|$ is a rescaled ground state.

nodes.name: reduction to constant phase
nodes.statement: The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $\mathbb{R}^N$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains to show the phase $w=v/|v|$ is constant.

nodes.name: phase is constant
nodes.statement:
Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $\mathrm{Re}(\overline{w}
abla w)\equiv 0$, thus \[ |
abla v|^2=|
abla(|v|)|^2+|v|^2|
abla w|^2+2|v|
abla(|v|)\cdot \mathrm{Re}(\overline{w}
abla w) \] and \[ \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2=\|
abla (|v|)\|_{L^2}^2+\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |v|^2|
abla w|^2dx. \] Together with Hardy's inequality, this implies that, if $|
abla w|
eq 0$ then $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction. Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Gradient splitting and Hardy's inequality: nonconstant phase would lower $J$.

nodes.name: plan of the proof
nodes.statement: The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $\mathbb{R}^N$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~\ref{charact.prop}.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: exclude (V),(D), localize translations, conclude via Proposition 3.

nodes.name: Step 1: compactness in $L^q$
nodes.statement: {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(\mathbb{R}^N)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Big\{\frac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}=\frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[ \begin{split} \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\leqslant\frac{1}{2}\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) -\frac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|dx \\ &\leqslant\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\leqslant 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (\ref{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\geqslant 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad \text{and} \quad E(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad\text{and}\quad H(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|z_k|^{p+1}dx\right)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$. Consequently, by Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ such that \begin{equation} \widetilde{v}_{n_k} \rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\mathbb{R}^N), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \widetilde{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\widetilde{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\widetilde{v}_{n_k}\rightharpoonup v$ weakly in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out vanishing and dichotomy; get $L^q$ compactness up to translations.

nodes.name: vanishing excluded
nodes.statement: First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Big\{\frac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}=\frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing forces positive energy, contradiction.

nodes.name: dichotomy excluded
nodes.statement: Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[ \begin{split} \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\leqslant\frac{1}{2}\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) -\frac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|dx \\ &\leqslant\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\leqslant 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (\ref{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\geqslant 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad \text{and} \quad E(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad\text{and}\quad H(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|z_k|^{p+1}dx\right)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Dichotomy forces both pieces to zero energy and $H$, contradiction.

nodes.name: compactness up to translation
nodes.statement: Consequently, by Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ such that \begin{equation} \widetilde{v}_{n_k} \rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\mathbb{R}^N), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \widetilde{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\widetilde{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\widetilde{v}_{n_k}\rightharpoonup v$ weakly in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.
nodes.statement_short: Case (C): translates converge in $L^q$ to $v$ with $\|v\|_2=M_{gs}$.

nodes.name: Step 2: localization
nodes.statement:
{\em Step~2: Localization.} We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|ightarrow\infty$ as $kightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}. We start by showing that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\geqslant R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$, there exists $C\geqslant0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\leqslant R^{-2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\leqslant CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$. Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\geqslant\delta. \end{equation*} Note that this inequality will still hold if we increase the value of $R$ or pass to a further subsequence. Let $a>0$ and $\varphi\in C_0^\infty([0,\infty))$ be such that $\varphi(r)=1$ for $0\leqslant r \leqslant R$, $\varphi(r)=0$ for $r\geqslant R+a$, $0\leqslant\varphi\leqslant1$ and $\|\varphi'\|_{L^\infty}\leqslant 1/a$.
